67: Most whole projects in Snohomish — a few rooms and the stairs — come to between $2,000 and $4,500. A 1,200 sq ft main floor plus its staircase usually reaches $5,500 to $8,500. 69: Snohomish is on the regular route, river flats to the hill above First Street. Out of the van come 20+ carpet samples, all three pad grades included, set down on the very floors they'd cover so color reads under your own windows instead of store lighting. Every room, stair and landing gets measured, and the written price is in your hands before the truck pulls away. You pay nothing for the visit.
71: Count on $99 per room in Snohomish. A power stretcher hauls ripples, buckles and trip spots back out at about a fifth of replacement cost. In houses that have had a century to settle, loose carpet is common — and stretching is the better spend as long as the pile hasn't given up and the color still fits the house.
79: The line is simple. Carpet whose pile still springs back, over sound backing, in a color you can live with, wants a $99-per-room stretch, not a tear-out. Move to new carpet once walk paths stay crushed, seams open up, backing turns brittle, or pet odor has outlasted the last professional cleaning. Plenty of Snohomish carpet is still on the right side of that line, and an estimator will say which before pricing anything.
83: Plank subfloors under a lot of Snohomish's older houses soak up whatever reaches them, and once that happens the smell never really leaves. The fix: a moisture-barrier pad beneath solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing. Backing and barrier together keep accidents off the wood, and the fiber takes a diluted-bleach cleanup without going pale. That pad upgrade runs from $0.65 per square foot, and samples of both ride along in the van.
85: Two warranties, from two different places. The mill covers the carpet — usually 10 to 25 years, wear and stain both, with the span set by grade — and OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty covers the install, which on an old Snohomish staircase is the half that earns its keep. Both are written into your quote. One catch: mills often tie coverage to a minimum pad, so all three pad grades ride out to the house.
